transcript.content: Hello. What brings you to the clinic today?

I keep cutting people off and jumping into things before they’re finished talking or deciding, and it’s starting to mess up my job and my money. I really need to figure out why I can't just wait my turn before I end up making a mistake I can't fix.
Have you struggled with these behaviors, like interrupting others and acting impulsively, since you were a child, or do they tend to come and go in phases?

It’s definitely been a constant struggle since I was a kid, not something that comes and goes. Even back in elementary school, I couldn't stay in my seat, constantly blurted out answers, and talked over my teachers. My report cards always had notes saying I was "overactive" and "disruptive," so it's been there my whole life.
Do you find that these difficulties with impulsivity and restlessness also cause problems in your personal life, such as at home or in your relationships with family and friends?

Yeah, it causes huge problems at home, especially with my wife; my constant fidgeting and restlessness during dinner or movies makes the whole family nervous. Plus, my habit of cutting her off and blurting out snap financial decisions before she can even finish talking has led to constant arguments and a lot of money stress.
Along with the restlessness and impulsivity, do you also struggle with focusing on details, organizing your tasks, or easily getting distracted?

Yes, I really do. At work, I'll blow past small details like skipping a torque step or misreading a decimal on a gauge, even when I'm trying hard to follow the checklist. And during conversations, my mind will just drift off halfway through while my wife or boss is talking, so I have to ask them to repeat themselves.

latest_inference.note: The patient has confirmed lifelong, pervasive symptoms of both hyperactivity/impulsivity (restlessness, interrupting, fidgeting) and inattention (difficulty focusing on details, mind drifting during conversations) causing significant impairment at work and home. This clinical picture fully aligns with ICD-10 F90.0 (Disturbance of activity and attention), and no further questioning is required.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a lifelong history of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity dating back to elementary school. These symptoms are pervasive, causing significant impairment across multiple domains, including his marriage, finances, and occupational performance. The clinical presentation is highly characteristic of Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Combined Presentation (ICD-10: F90.0).
